The 2027 Nissan Rogue Hybrid Is Now on Sale in the US, but Only in SR Technology Package Flavor
16 photos
Photo: Nissan
Finally available to configure in the US market, Nissan's heavily anticipated Rogue Hybrid is heavily restricted at launch. While its build & price tool may read $35,490 for the base SV grade, prospective customers are presented with a pricier trim level for the time being.
SR with the SR Technology Package is how said configuration is called, and the $41,490 starting price does not include $1,575 for destination and delivery. Both the SV and the range-topping Platinum don't reach showrooms until January 2027. Even so, the sole trim level available right now loads the compact-sized crossover with a lot of desirable stuff.
I find the single-trim launch approach rather interesting because most automakers either launch the best- or least-equipped model first. Nissan , by comparison, put a feature-rich version of the Rogue Hybrid in front of the first wave of customers. The SR Technology Package adds $4,000 to the SR's advertised price, with that money getting you better tech and more convenience.
To understand what you're getting, let's first run through some SR highlights: quilted TailorFit seating, 19-inch alloys, dual 12.3-inch screens for instrumentation and infotainment, Apple CarPlay, and Android Auto. Both wireless, of course! Opting for the SR Technology Package upgrades the tech side of the cabin to 14.3 inches for both screens.
Google built-in goodies, a memory driver's seat, memory outside mirrors, a power liftgate, panoramic roof, plus advanced ProPILOT Assist functionality also need mentioning. Said package further includes 3D HD Enhanced Intelligent Around View Monitor with Invisible Hood View and Front Wide View, a heated steering wheel, rear automatic braking, front and rear parking sensors, and gloss-black roof rails. In other words, $4,000 does get you a lot of things.
Photo: Nissan Every grade ships with standard all-wheel drive, and every grade of the Rogue Hybrid relies on a 1.5-liter turbo inline-three without the VC-Turbo nonsense of the combustion-only Rogue. Gifted with a fixed 13.0:1 compression ratio, this mill is used exclusively for generating electricity, making the Rogue Hybrid stand out from conventional hybrid crossovers.
Said engine is tuned for a narrow operating window that prioritizes efficiency over power. Its thermal efficiency is very high, with Nissan claiming a 42% thermal efficiency. Going forward, Nissan hopes to achieve 50% in the coming years through advancements in ultra-lean burn combustion, strict fixed-point operation, and comprehensive waste heat recovery.
Good for up to 225 horsepower in optimal conditions, the Rogue Hybrid uses two electric motors and a 1.67-kWh battery pack. There is no charging plug to speak of, as that would defeat the purpose of a hybrid. Optimized for its charge and discharge ability, said battery works together with the internal combustion engine to keep those electric drive units spinning.
Advertised with the quietest and quickest acceleration in the class, the Rogue Hybrid also promises best-in-class braking from 60 miles per hour (97 kilometers per hour) to zero. As far as fuel economy is concerned, the EPA-estimated figures are 41 miles per gallon in the city and 36 on the highway.
That's 38 mpg (6.2 l/100 km) combined versus a best of 31 (7.6) for the internal combustion Rogue with all-wheel drive or 32 (7.4) with front-wheel drive. Unfortunately, the combined 38-mpg estimate isn't good enough by Toyota standards. The EPA lists 42 mpg (5.6 l/100 km) for the RAV4 Hybrid with all-wheel drive, and that rival is the single best-selling hybrid crossover in the US as of this writing.
